sentence: This project studies how astrocytes in the retina and optic nerve support blood vessels and help the optic nerve become myelinated.
This project gets a radiotherapy system to study whether ultra-high dose rate radiotherapy spares normal tissue while still controlling tumors.
This project studies how signaling proteins in a T cell handle information from its receptors and how the cell perceives an antigenic agonist.
This project studies how circular pieces of DNA outside the chromosomes form, work and help cancer cells resist treatment.
This project builds speech-based tools that predict whether people with psychosis will return to hospital or stop treatment.
This project uses CRISPR gene editing to try to correct a harmful change in a gene that causes phenylketonuria, directly in the liver.
This project studies how damaged blood vessels drive long-lasting inflammation around dental implants and tests whether existing drugs can repair the damage.
This project builds gene-editing tools for Candida albicans to find genes that help this fungus resist antifungal drugs.
This project builds imaging agents and treatments that detect and promote a tumor environment where immune cells can act, in breast and pancreatic cancer models.
This project studies how metastatic colorectal cancer cells show peptides on their surface and how these change in advanced disease.
This project studies what two genes linked to type 1 diabetes do in beta-cells and whether targeting them could improve beta-cell function.
This project studies whether intestinal stem cells keep an epigenetic memory of inflammation caused by a parasitic helminth infection.
This project builds a tool that uses chest CT images to predict who benefits from immunotherapy and who is at risk of pneumonitis.
This project studies how signaling pathways control the formation and repair of dentin, using genetically engineered mouse models and dental mesenchymal cells.
This project studies how epigenetic control in trophoblast stem cells shapes the different cell types needed to form a healthy placenta.
This project uses mouse and rat models of bronchopulmonary dysplasia to test whether gene delivery or cell therapy can improve lung repair in neonatal animals.
This project uses data and samples from birth cohorts to find genetic variants in mothers and children linked to fetal alcohol spectrum disorders.
This project tries to turn fibroblasts directly into urothelial stem cells for the bladder.
This project tests whether a sparse total-body positron emission tomography scanner can make dynamic images nearly as accurate as a full system.
